ranking.name: Water leaving the land (evapotranspiration)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water leaving the land (evapotranspiration) in Siberia changed by +0.065 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval +0.038 to +0.093), which is statistically significant (p < 0.001). Over the whole 24.7-year period that is an increase of about 0.160 mm/day.

ranking.name: Rain and snow (precipitation)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, rain and snow (precipitation) in Siberia changed by +0.061 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval +0.032 to +0.090), which is statistically significant (p < 0.001). Over the whole 24.7-year period that is an increase of about 0.150 mm/day.

ranking.name: Water in the topsoil
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water in the topsoil in Siberia shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.17): the estimate is −0.28 kg/m² per decade (95% confidence interval −0.68 to +0.12). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.
